title: Research: audit connector-covering-code's parity-capacity filter and its simple-word boundary
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Add `research/connector-capacity-parity-audit/`, a scoped proof and independent implementation audit of `Engine::capacity`, the parity-capacity filter in conorholds' retained `connector-covering-code` source (its simple length-22 exclusion).

The predicate is necessary for simple restored universal words in its four-low/three-high projection, including repeated low vertices: the pair counts include pairs between different blocks at the same low vertex. Direct position-pair enumeration agrees with the actual compiled predicate on **791,827 declared gap inputs**; **53,379 pass the capacity relaxation**, with no claim that these are realizable words. The proof also identifies sixteen low-linear parity changes that preserve the verdict; full-word time parity is one of them.

A concrete scope control matters: the credited universal word `010201030102010345464546` has 24 steps and 23 distinct prefixes. The predicate rejects it because nine positions at low zero represent only eight distinct high states. This disproves extending the predicate to arbitrary restored words; it is **not a predecessor bug or a counterexample to the length-22 exclusion**. The predecessor excludes repeated-prefix length-22 candidates by separate arguments (sections 2 and 3 of its README) and applies this filter only to simple cycles.

The package reconstructs #2973's `01021323` as credited calibration and pins the affected #2542/#2634/#2691 call sites. Their old bit-0-filter receipts remain invalid exclusion evidence; #2973/#3005 supply separate corrected evidence already on main. This audit neither reruns those complete censuses nor establishes the successor's complete `f(7)=24` claim. No supplier, tariff, selected frontier or kappa change.

The claim is in [discussion #1317, comment 19001874](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1317#discussioncomment-19001874), following #2973's released length-22 question and its newer main successor. Full structured task metadata is in `TASK.json`.

It is not a second complete B exclusion.

## Validation

On CPython 3.12.3 and GCC C++ 13.3.0, the registered replay (ordinary and optimized `verify.py`, then `check_failure_controls.py`) passed in 14.703 seconds, and the metadata/pins and committed-byte checks pass:

```sh
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/connector-capacity-parity-audit --check-only
python3 -I -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/connector-capacity-parity-audit
python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/connector-capacity-parity-audit
```

Observed from the registered replay:

```text
PASS_CONNECTOR_CAPACITY_PARITY cases=791827 accepted=53379 positive_projections=176 gauges=2816 python_queries=1282 repeated_prefix_control=1 no_full_census
PASS_CONNECTOR_CAPACITY_PARITY cases=791827 accepted=53379 positive_projections=176 gauges=2816 python_queries=1282 repeated_prefix_control=1 no_full_census
PASS_CAPACITY_FAILURE_CONTROLS source_pin=1 native_mutants=2 malformed_query=2 receipt=1
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/connector-capacity-parity-audit outcome=completed
```

Evidence:

- 791,827 native/source-oracle comparisons, no disagreement; exact domain sizes independently computed by generating-function coefficients or closed counts.
- 176 genuine universal simple 24-step projections pass, including 120 with repeated low vertices; 2,816 parity-bucket permutation checks.
- 1,282 separately specified Python/native queries; the universal repeated-prefix boundary is additionally checked against the actual predicate.
- Parity-reset and omitted-equal-low-pair mutants change 1,148 and 542 B-core verdicts. The two explicit fixtures change `C(6,1)` from 4 to 3 and `C(0,0)` from 6 to 2; these are gap fixtures, not word witnesses.
- Actual native parity-reset and relaxed-fiber-cap mutations discriminate in private copies. Source hash changes, a corrupted fresh receipt and truncated native queries reject. These checks also run with Python `-O`.
- All four native domain rows match under AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer with no diagnostics (`-O1 -g -fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-omit-frame-pointer`).
- Eight exact predecessor-head byte comparisons, package metadata/pins, `git diff --check`, and committed-byte preflight for all 18 package/input files pass.

No hosted CI, complete n=7 word census, full successor proof, published classification proof, formal-kernel check or independent human review is claimed. The source template generator supplies the 82 tested low templates; this audit does not prove that generator complete. Remaining path tables, propagation, symmetry reductions, non-simple branch and physical/all-size obligations remain open to separate review.

## Credit

Prepared for commdata2338 (@commdata2338), with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. conorholds supplied the successor predicate, finite exclusion and simple 24-step fixture; Nicholas Stone supplied #2691/#2973 and the tiny counterexample; Nick Petalas supplied #3005; Aaron Wang supplied #2542/#2634 and later set-level work. Ross Richardson supplied the #943 model. Douglas Colkitt (@Mister-Meeseeks) supplied #1185 and the retained Gray upper witness. James Reed (jwr) supplied the earlier #3096 tiny audit; its calibration is not presented as new. Apache-2.0 and predecessor attribution are preserved.

**AI assistance:** submitted by @commdata2338 with substantial AI assistance. OpenAI Codex (GPT-6 Astra) did the derivation, the implementation, the checking and the writing; it was packaged and submitted with Claude Code. No independent human review is claimed.

## Open next questions

Independently check the successor's remaining B path-domain propagation rules with explicit endpoint, same-low disjointness and conditional-coverage controls. Only after those pass should a separately budgeted complete B replay be proposed. The published covering/classification premises and non-simple branch remain distinct obligations; this predicate proof cannot discharge them.
